events.title: Lightning Destroys the Spire of Old St Paul's
events.description: The towering spire of Old St Paul's Cathedral in London was destroyed by fire. The blaze followed a lightning strike. The cathedral was one of the tallest and most prominent buildings in Tudor England.
events.significance: The loss changed the London skyline for good, because the spire was never rebuilt. The cathedral itself was later destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666.

events.title: Congress Passes the Women's Suffrage Amendment
events.description: The U.S. Congress approved the amendment that guaranteed American women the right to vote. It then sent the amendment to the states for ratification.
events.significance: The measure became the 19th Amendment in 1920. It was a landmark victory after decades of campaigning by the suffrage movement.

events.title: The Battle of Midway Begins
events.description: Japanese Admiral Chuichi Nagumo ordered a strike on Midway Atoll, opening one of the most important naval battles of World War II in the Pacific.
events.significance: The battle became a turning point in the Pacific war. It shifted the balance of naval power away from Japan.

events.title: Tiananmen Square Protests Suppressed
events.description: China's People's Liberation Army moved against pro-democracy demonstrators in Beijing and cleared Tiananmen Square. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
events.significance: The crackdown ended weeks of mass demonstrations. It remains a powerful symbol of the struggle for political freedom, and its memory is still tightly controlled in China.
